issues.failure_explanation: The layer components solve homogeneous discrete equations, so the data-quadrature cancellation (the T3/T4 mechanism) that makes the scheme second order is unavailable. In the coarse-x region (ρ_{i,j} = āh_i/ε ≫ 1, i.e. ε ≪ N^{-1}) the fitted operator degenerates to upwinding, since εσ(−ρ) ≈ 0 and the x-part tends to āD^-_x. Applying it to the exact layer (Lw_N = 0, i.e. ā w_{N,x} − ε w_{N,yy} = ε w_{N,xx}) gives by Taylor expansion L^N w_N = (ε − āh_i/2)w_{N,xx} + O(h_i² + εk_j² terms) ≈ −(āh_i/2)w_{N,xx}; by the paper's own bounds |w_{N,xx}| ≤ Ce^{−(1−y)/√ε} = O(1) at mesh points inside the characteristic layer. Hence |L^N(W_N−w_N)| = Θ(N^{-1}) there — first order in h_i, with no x-decay — whereas the claimed bound is ≤ CM^{-2}(ln M)² + CN^{-4}/ε in the coarse region (using e^{−α(1−x_i)/ε} ≤ N^{-2}), smaller than the actual value by a factor of order N/(ln N)² for M = N. The claimed truncation bound is therefore false, and applying the discrete minimum principle to the true residual (e.g. with the barrier Ch e^{2x_i/α}Φ(y_j)) yields only |W_N−w_N| ≤ CN^{-1}; the same holds for W_S−w_S. Thus Lemma 5's stated bound, and with it the N-rate of Theorem main-result, fail for data permitted by Assumption (assume) whose characteristic-layer boundary data is not affine in x: the scheme is first-order accurate on these components, the same order as the upwind scheme of [hemkerb] that the paper claims to improve on. (The numerical tables remain consistent with this, since the first-order term has a small constant masked by larger second-order constants in the computed range.)
